projects.title: Airfoil method hierarchy validation
projects.summary: Analytical and Hess–Smith predictions are checked against one traceable NASA NACA 0012 series, with inviscid blind spots kept visible.
methods: Thin-airfoil theory and Prandtl–Glauert correction at Mach 0.15.
Cosine-spaced Hess–Smith source/vortex panels with a Kutta condition.
Linear-range comparison and 40/80/160/240-panel refinement.
limitations: One symmetric airfoil, Reynolds number, Mach number, and transition condition.
Potential flow cannot predict boundary layers, viscous drag, separation, or stall.
The validation range is explicitly limited to -4.1 through 10.2 degrees.
commands: cd projects/airfoil-methods && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

claims.statement: Panel-model lift RMSE remains below 0.1 inside the declared linear range.

projects.title: Dimensionless numbers toolkit with dimensional guards
projects.summary: Reynolds, Mach, Prandtl, Nusselt, Grashof and Rayleigh computed under strict SI dimension checks, with a property table anchored to Incropera's textbook tables.
methods: Defining equations implemented in expanded form so the Ra = Gr * Pr identity is a genuine check.
SI dimension-vector guards reject dimensionally inconsistent or non-physical inputs with explicit errors.
Property table: piecewise-linear lookup, exact at anchors transcribed from Incropera 7th ed. Tables A.4/A.6.
limitations: Constant-property table: five anchors for air and water, linear interpolation, no extrapolation.
Incompressible-regime scope; no real-gas effects beyond the perfect-gas speed of sound.
Regime-limit annotations in the sweep figure are intuition, not transition predictions.
commands: cd projects/dimensionless-numbers && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

sources.title: Incropera, DeWitt, Bergman & Lavine (2011), Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, 7th ed., Tables A.4/A.6
NIST Chemistry WebBook, Thermophysical Properties of Fluid Systems

claims.statement: The 15 m/s, 0.3 m chord reference Reynolds number equals the hand calculation to machine precision.
Ra = Gr * Pr holds to machine precision across 500 seeded random input draws.
Every intentionally invalid call in the guard suite is rejected.
Every tabulated property anchor is reproduced exactly by table lookup.

projects.title: F1 2026 full-car CFD pilot
projects.summary: A deliberately coarse full-car pilot verifies geometry preparation, meshing, solving, convergence analysis, and per-part force extraction before production compute is claimed.
methods: Fourteen STEP parts are converted and repaired for an OpenFOAM half-car external-flow workflow.
A corrected one-million-cell pilot is advanced for 400 steady iterations with moving-ground and staged numerical controls.
A batch-means confidence-interval criterion selects the averaging window for drag and lift coefficients.
A zero-failure gate now covers nineteen OpenFOAM mesh outcomes plus one external volume-topology attempt, including bounded surface repair and a discrete-STL Gmsh route, before solver launch.
limitations: The published coefficients are pipeline-validation values from a coarse pilot, not production aerodynamic predictions.
The 25–35 million-cell baseline and mesh/model sensitivity programme have not run.
The third-party geometry is reconstructed from public imagery and is not official team CAD.

All twenty bounded qualification paths failed: the best uniform-envelope topology retains eight face-interior skew failures, both tested repaired-surface meshes retain fifteen, and Gmsh generates no volume elements from the overlapping discrete boundary.

claims.statement: The corrected pilot drag mean has a relative 95 percent batch-means confidence interval below one percent.
The corrected pilot lift mean has a relative 95 percent batch-means confidence interval below one percent.
Total force coefficients and all six declared component groups are present in the corrected pilot output.
The divergent front-wing boundary-layer trial remains visible rather than being presented as valid aerodynamic evidence.
The portfolio does not claim that the production 25–35 million-cell baseline has completed.
All controlled front-wing qualification meshes remain rejected; none is promoted to a solver or production mesh.
The qualification evidence covers twenty bounded paths: nineteen OpenFOAM mesh outcomes and one external topology attempt.
The repaired front-wing surface nearest the 0.1 mm deviation budget still fails the strict mesh gate.
The discrete-STL Gmsh alternative writes zero volume elements from the overlapping boundary.

Public geometry and half-car symmetry prohibit team-level absolute predictions, yaw and physical correlation claims.

claims.statement: Nine retained pilot variants pass their declared validity gates.
Both diverged roughness runs remain visible and excluded from comparison.
The retained baseline has positive drag and negative lift under the published convention.
Pilot mesh sensitivity remains material and blocks production absolute claims.

Centerline interpolation against Ghia, Ghia and Shin reference values.

Validation covers one Reynolds number and one canonical internal-flow geometry.
Browser speed and lattice time are not physical vehicle-flow predictions.

projects.title: FlowROM reduced-order validation

projects.title: FSAE cooling system screen
projects.summary: Coupled air, hydraulic, and transient thermal models test a candidate FSAE cooling loop and preserve the engineering no-go decision.
methods: Published component curves are digitised and coupled at matched air and hydraulic operating points.
An 80-cell finite-volume coolant model resolves baseline, 10-second peak, and recovery phases.
Spatial and time-step studies quantify numerical sensitivity before the system decision is published.
A four-grid OpenFOAM fan-jump/porous-core surrogate qualifies the numerical coupling without claiming installed-vehicle CFD.
limitations: The CWA150 curve remains secondary-hosted and is conservatively biased; final approval requires first-party or measured hydraulic data.
Motor liquid heat fraction and KW26 operating-point loss remain uncertain and are swept rather than invented.
This is a coolant-domain screen, not solid-component conjugate heat transfer or a completed vehicle installation.
The OpenFOAM case is a shrouded proxy with no installed sidepod, wheel, leakage or measured boundary conditions.

projects.title: Ground-effect image-vortex validation
projects.summary: A from-primitives horseshoe-vortex solver isolates finite-wing ground effect and checks boundary enforcement, asymptotic recovery, analytical scale, and panel refinement.
methods: Finite Biot-Savart segments assembled into one-row horseshoe-vortex lattices.
Reversed image vortices enforce a moving ground plane without a viscous road boundary layer.
Ride-height sweep, Trefftz-plane induced drag, analytical scale check, and span refinement.
limitations: The model is linear, inviscid, steady, incompressible, and zero-thickness.
There are no tyres, body, diffuser, leakage, separation, or moving-road boundary layer.
The published sweep stops at quarter-chord height h/c=0.25 and is not a race-car performance prediction.

projects.title: 2-D unsteady heat diffusion: explicit FTCS with analytical validation
projects.summary: A first time-dependent PDE solver: explicit FTCS heat diffusion on a uniform grid, validated against the analytical slab transient with a hard stability gate and an exact energy-conservation identity.
methods: Cell-centred finite-volume FTCS on a uniform square grid with Dirichlet and zero-flux Neumann boundaries.
Hard stability gate: runs with r = alpha*dt/dx^2 > 0.25 are refused and logged before integration.
Quasi-1-D validation against the analytical slab series truncated at a 1e-14 envelope tolerance.
Temporal order isolated by refinement against a fine-time reference on a fixed grid.
limitations: Explicit scheme: the stability bound forces dt to shrink with dx^2.
Constant isotropic diffusivity; no advection, sources, or phase change.
Cartesian uniform grids with square cells only.
First order in time, second order in space; the temporal-order check uses a fine-time reference because the analytical error couples space and time truncation.
commands: cd projects/heat-diffusion-2d && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

sources.title: Weisstein, Heat Conduction Equation — Wolfram MathWorld
sources.role: analytical reference equation and separation-of-variables solution form

claims.statement: The quasi-1-D FTCS transient matches the analytical slab series with L-infinity error below 5e-5 at t = 0.05 s on a 100x20 grid.
Temporal refinement at fixed grid shows first-order convergence: the observed order stays within 0.1 of 1.
A fully insulated run conserves cell-integrated energy with relative drift below 1e-12.
The solver refuses and logs an attempted run at r = 0.26, above the FTCS limit 0.25.

projects.title: Pipe flow sizing with verified friction and pump intersection
projects.summary: Darcy-Weisbach friction, Newton-solved Colebrook, series-network closure, and a pump operating point checked against identities, residuals, and the published Swamee-Jain band.
methods: Laminar Darcy friction f=64/Re below Re=2300.
Colebrook equation solved by Newton iteration from a Haaland initial guess.
Minor losses via summed K coefficients; series-network flow by monotone bisection.
Pump/system operating point by Newton with central-difference derivative, cross-checked by brute-force scan.
limitations: Steady, incompressible, single-phase flow only; no transients or compressibility.
No cavitation or NPSH modelling.
K coefficients are declared handbook order-of-magnitude values with wide published uncertainty.
The pump curve is a declared quadratic model, not vendor data.
Hard laminar/turbulent switch at Re=2300; series topology only.
commands: cd projects/pipe-flow-sizing && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

sources.title: Swamee & Jain (1976), Explicit Equations for Pipe-Flow Problems, ASCE J. Hydraulics Division 102(5)
sources.role: explicit friction formula with published +/-3% accuracy band

sources.title: Haaland (1983), Simple and Explicit Formulas for the Friction Factor in Turbulent Pipe Flow, ASME J. Fluids Engineering 105(1)
sources.role: explicit initial guess for the Newton iteration

sources.title: Colebrook (1939), Turbulent Flow in Pipes, J. Institution of Civil Engineers 11(4)

claims.statement: The laminar branch reproduces 64/Re with absolute error at most 1e-12 over a 200-point grid on Re in [100, 2300].
The Newton Colebrook solution keeps the implicit-equation residual below 1e-12 across a 150-point Reynolds/roughness grid.
Colebrook solutions agree with the explicit Swamee-Jain formula within its published +/-3% band across its declared validity range.
The pump/system intersection residual stays below 1e-10 Pa and the solution lands inside the independent brute-force bracket.

projects.title: Potential-flow sandbox: complex potentials and cylinder superposition
projects.summary: Elementary complex potentials superposed into cylinder flow with circulation, verified against analytical Cp, stagnation, circulation, streamfunction, and Kutta-Joukowski identities.
methods: Complex-potential elementary flows (uniform, source/sink, doublet, vortex) with dW/dz = u - iv.
Superposed flow past a circular cylinder with imposed circulation, positive clockwise.
Fixed-step RK4 streamline tracing checked against the analytical streamfunction Im(W).
limitations: Inviscid, irrotational, incompressible, and strictly two-dimensional: no boundary layer, separation, or wake.
Circulation is imposed, not predicted; no Kutta condition selects it.
Zero drag is a property of the model class (d'Alembert), not a prediction.

projects.title: Steady 1-D conduction with finite differences
projects.summary: The first discretised PDE in the study sequence: a generating rod with a convective tip, solved with a from-scratch Thomas algorithm and verified against closed-form and manufactured solutions.
methods: Node-centred finite differences with a half-control-volume Robin tip.
Thomas algorithm implemented from scratch for the tridiagonal solve.
Closed-form exact solution, manufactured-solution grid-convergence study, and conservative global energy balance.
limitations: One-dimensional, steady state with constant thermal properties.
No contact resistance at either boundary; tip radiation is excluded.
The quadratic physical solution is reproduced to roundoff, so the convergence order is demonstrated on a manufactured source term.
